job.title: Senior Engineer, Commerce
job.description:
Fox Tech desarrolla los productos digitales detrás de las marcas de deportes y entretenimiento de FOX. Nuestras aplicaciones funcionan en web, móvil y dispositivos de sala de estar, y millones de personas las usan, generalmente todas al mismo tiempo cuando comienza un partido. Esos picos de tráfico determinan cómo construimos todo.

Estamos contratando ingenieros para construir la próxima generación de nuestros productos de streaming.

Te unirás al equipo de Comercio, que es responsable de los sistemas que manejan el dinero: pagos, impuestos, facturación y suscripciones en todos nuestros productos directos al consumidor. Un error aquí cuesta dólares reales, y un checkout lento cuesta un suscriptor, por lo que el estándar de corrección y disponibilidad es más alto que en casi cualquier otra parte de la infraestructura.

La mayor parte del trabajo ocurre detrás de la interfaz de checkout: autorización y captura de pagos; reembolsos, disputas y reconciliación; el ciclo de vida de las suscripciones, incluyendo renovaciones, upgrades, downgrades, cancelaciones y todos los estados intermedios; idempotencia y procesamiento de webhooks contra APIs de proveedores que reintentan, llegan fuera de orden y a veces “mienten”; cálculo de impuestos a través de proveedores externos; y el alcance de PCI DSS, manteniendo los datos sensibles de los clientes donde deben estar.

Trabajarás con stakeholders de distintas áreas de negocio de FOX, que no todas venden de la misma forma ni al mismo público. Parte del trabajo consiste en construir capacidades de comercio que puedan reutilizarse entre ellas sin homogeneizar la experiencia de cada una.

El ecosistema de desarrollo ha cambiado drásticamente en los últimos dos años, y nosotros hemos cambiado con él. Nuestros ingenieros usan agentes de código y herramientas de IA generativa como parte de su flujo de trabajo normal, no como un experimento ocasional. Esperamos que llegues con fluidez real: que sepas en qué casos estas herramientas son confiables y en cuáles no lo son, y que ya tengas tus propios hábitos para revisar, probar y proteger lo que producen.

Las herramientas en sí seguirán cambiando. Lo que funcionaba hace seis meses ya está desactualizado, y lo que estandaricemos este trimestre probablemente no será lo que usemos el próximo año. Buscamos ingenieros que vean esto como algo normal y que estén dispuestos a seguir replanteando su propio flujo de trabajo.

Para ser claros sobre el estándar: las herramientas de IA elevan lo que esperamos de ti, no lo reducen. Tú eres responsable del código, de las decisiones de diseño y del comportamiento en producción, sin importar quién (o qué) escribió el primer borrador.

  • Liderar la dirección técnica de las principales capacidades de comercio, desde el diseño hasta la operación en producción.
  • Liderar discusiones de arquitectura y tomar las decisiones de compromiso entre confiabilidad, costo, seguridad y velocidad de entrega.
  • Escribir código de alta calidad con cobertura de pruebas significativa y automatización.
  • Asumir la responsabilidad de producción: respuesta a incidentes, análisis de causa raíz y el trabajo de seguimiento que evita que el mismo incidente vuelva a ocurrir.
  • Mentorear a otros ingenieros y elevar el estándar de ingeniería del equipo.
  • Evaluar tecnologías emergentes de pagos y comercio, y argumentar a favor de cambios que mejoren de forma medible la conversión, la confiabilidad o el costo operativo.
  • Comercio se mantiene estable durante los grandes eventos en vivo, cuando el tráfico llega todo de una vez.
  • Los cambios de pagos y suscripciones se lanzan de forma segura, y puedes señalar la métrica que se movió.
  • Otras áreas de negocio de FOX pueden construir sobre tu trabajo sin heredar el flujo de checkout de otro equipo.
  • Licenciatura en Ciencias de la Computación, o experiencia equivalente.
  • 5+ años de experiencia en ingeniería de software, con enfoque en APIs escalables y seguras, y sistemas basados en eventos.
  • Sólido dominio de Go. Nuestros servicios de comercio están escritos casi en su totalidad en Go, y necesitamos que empieces a escribir código de producción en este lenguaje desde el inicio.
  • Experiencia demostrable usando herramientas de IA generativa en desarrollo de software profesional. Puedes explicar dónde mejoraron tu flujo de trabajo, dónde introdujeron riesgos, y cómo revisas, pruebas y proteges el código asistido por IA.
  • Experiencia en el dominio de comercio. Has trabajado con Stripe, Adyen, Braintree o similares, y entiendes cómo se conectan las piezas entre sí.
  • Bases sólidas de ciencias de la computación e instintos fuertes de resolución de problemas.
  • Experiencia con decisiones de diseño y arquitectura de software a gran escala.
  • Sólida experiencia con SQL y NoSQL, idealmente DynamoDB y Redis.
  • Experiencia profesional con AWS u otro proveedor de nube.
  • Experiencia práctica con contenedores y Kubernetes.
  • Nuestros sistemas dan soporte a eventos en vivo y nuestro equipo está distribuido globalmente, por lo que el puesto implica algo de trabajo fuera del horario habitual: llamadas programadas entre regiones, además de respuesta a incidentes durante eventos importantes.
  • Aplicaciones de streaming, especialmente aquellas que manejan eventos en vivo a gran escala.
  • Comercio electrónico, particularmente tráfico de alta disponibilidad en eventos como Black Friday.
  • Gestión del ciclo de vida de suscripciones: renovaciones, upgrades, downgrades y cancelaciones.
  • Idempotencia, procesamiento de webhooks, reintentos y consistencia eventual.
  • Comercio integrado directamente en una experiencia de streaming de video. Si has explorado esto, nos gustaría saberlo.

job.title: Manager, Technical Projects & Innovation
job.description:
FOX Sports Remote Engineering & Operations runs a standing portfolio of technical initiatives — private 5G at venues, in-helmet point-of-view cameras, camera tracking and augmented reality, connected-ball and player tracking, volumetric capture, and automated content moderation. Most of them are technically sound and short of hands. This role exists to move them.

This is a hands-on job. You will spend a real share of your week doing the work yourself — on-site testing, integration, writing specifications, chasing vendors to a decision. You will also be the person who makes sure the rest of it happens: that every project has a next milestone and a date, that equipment was specified early enough to actually be ordered, and that the people who needed to know were told before it affected them.

If you're looking for a role that sets technology strategy from a distance, this isn't it. If you want to ship things that end up on air across NFL, MLB, College Football, NASCAR, UFL, and International Soccer, it is.

Stated plainly so expectations are clear from the start: this role executes, recommends, and escalates. Cross-sport technical architecture and vendor strategy sit with our Director of Engineering; remote integration and the plant interface sit with our Remote Integration Engineering lead; capital authority sits with the SVP. You'll work as a peer to both — they set the technical direction, you carry it to completion. That division is deliberate, and it means you can be excellent at this job without having to be the deepest engineer in the department.

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Drive our active technical initiatives to their next milestones — on-site tests and evaluations, vendor and partner coordination, and a live date on every card
  • Escalate the calls that need executive judgment quickly rather than letting a project sit while a decision waits
  • Produce specifications, equipment lists, and build calendars early enough that our integration and logistics function can procure and ship against real lead times rather than against deadlines
  • Support major capital projects from requirements through commissioning, in partnership with the teams that own integration and procurement
  • Apply and document the engineering standards our Director of Engineering sets, and hold new builds to them
  • When a property wants an exception, capture it, assess it, and raise it — rather than absorbing it quietly and letting the standard erode
  • Own the status reporting this function has been missing: where projects stand, what's at risk, what decisions are needed, and by when
  • Act as the Field Operations point of contact with our information security team, own the Field Operations security dashboard, and drive remediation items to closure under the security architecture our Director of Engineering owns
  • Give every initiative in the portfolio a next milestone and a date — and surface the stalled ones rather than letting them sit
  • Stand up status reporting that partners come to rely on
  • Get technical requirements to integration and logistics inside their lead times, every time.
  • Document the engineering standards as they exist today, with exceptions logged rather than absorbed.
  • Take the security dashboard fully in hand and bring remediation current
  • Take enough execution off our senior engineering staff that architecture and standards work can actually get done

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 5+ years in broadcast or live production engineering, with at least one or two leading projects or people
  • track record of getting technical projects across the line — including the unglamorous parts: vendor follow-through, lead times, and closing items out — we have deep technical expertise in the group; what we need alongside it is someone who converts decisions into finished work on a date.
  • Hands-on capability across IP video infrastructure (ST 2110, JPEG XS), RF and wireless camera systems, transmission, and remote production workflows — enough to earn credibility and do the work, without needing to be the deepest technical voice in the room
  • Judgment to work as a peer to senior technical colleagues: taking architectural direction from them while holding them to dates, and escalating rather than absorbing when the two conflict
  • Comfort working in a union environment
  • Written communication strong enough that people actually read your status and act on it
  • Willingness to travel and work event schedules, including nights, weekends, and holidays — expect heavier load during football season and around major events.

HOW WE'LL MEASURE SUCCESS

  • Every initiative in the portfolio has an owner, a milestone, and a date — and nothing sits stalled without being surfaced.
  • Partners describe communication from this function as predictable
  • Technical requirements reach integration and logistics within lead times
  • Projects delivered on schedule, with exceptions to standard logged rather than absorbed
  • Security remediation is current rather than accumulating
  • Measurably less execution work sitting with the Director of Engineering at year-end than at the start

job.description:
#WeAreParamount on a mission to unleash the power of content… you in?

Director, Analytics Engineer, Content and Subscriber Data

 

46418

 

Overview and Responsibilities

 

Paramount Streaming is a division of Paramount that encompasses both free, paid, and premium streaming services including Paramount+ and Pluto TV.

We are the Global Content and Lifecycle Analytics team, part of the Paramount Streaming, Data & Insights Group (DIG) team. DIG is a key connector among the Paramount Streaming verticals. The group consists of experts in various fields. They prototype, build, and scale data infrastructure and products. They assess, aggregate, and analyze data. They also create both qualitative and quantitative insights. This helps stakeholders by providing decision support, clear performance information, and actionable recommendations.

 

Role Details:

 

Paramount is seeking a Director of Analytics Engineering to lead the Content & Subscriber Analytics Engineering team within the Content & Lifecycle Analytics function. In this important management role, you will create the technical vision and strategy for two key data areas: content and subscriber data. You will also build and lead a team. This team will convert raw metadata, viewing data, and subscription events into reliable datasets, dashboards, and useful insights.

You will work closely with senior leaders in different areas. These areas include content operations and programming. They also cover licensing, subscriber growth, and retention. Additionally, they involve billing operations, product development, and engineering. Your goal is to ensure the organization has reliable and well-managed content and subscriber data. This data will help with decision-making for Paramount+, Pluto TV, and Paramount's overall streaming portfolio. This role is ideal for a hands-on leader who has built and scaled analytics engineering teams and wants to own data strategy across both domains at once.

Responsibilities Build, lead, and grow a team of analytics engineers and analysts covering both content metadata and subscriber data domains. Set technical strategy and roadmap for content and subscriber data infrastructure, balancing near-term stakeholder needs with long-term platform investment.

Establish and champion coding standards, data governance practices, and documentation norms across the team.

Partner with engineering, product, and business executive team to align data priorities with company strategy. Own the strategy and plan for two key areas. The first area is content metadata pipelines. This includes title catalogs, rights and licensing windows, genres, talent, franchise/series hierarchies, and availability. The second area is subscriber data pipelines. This covers acquisition, plan tier and pricing changes, billing status, and cancellation or win-back events. Ensure we have reliable data models for both areas. This includes content metadata models for precise title, franchise, and window reporting. It also includes subscriber models that cover the whole subscriber lifecycle. These models will help us analyze retention, churn, and lifetime value. Drive data quality initiatives in both areas. Identify and fix issues like duplicate titles, conflicting rights windows, and incorrect taxonomy tagging in content. Also, tackle billing discrepancies, plan misclassification, and duplicate accounts on the subscriber side. Contribute to anomaly detection systems and operational dashboards that track content catalog health, subscriber funnel performance, and data quality KPIs across both domains.

 

Basic Qualifications:

 

Bachelor’s degree in economics, Statistics, Analytics, Computer Science, MIS, Data Engineering, or related field or equivalent experience. 10+ years of experience in analytical engineering, data engineering, or data analytics, including experience managing or leading a team.

Solid SQL and data modeling expertise, with deep knowledge of ETL/ELT principles, data architecture, and performance optimization. Proven track record building and scaling data platforms and pipelines using tools such as Databricks, Airflow, Spark, or similar. You should have direct experience with content metadata. This includes title catalogs, rights and windowing data. It also includes genre or talent taxonomies. Comparable structured entertainment or media data is also acceptable. You must have direct experience with subscriber and subscription data. This experience includes working with acquisition, billing, plan tiers, and churn or retention events. You should have worked in a subscription or direct-to-consumer business. You should be able to influence senior stakeholders from various functions. You must also turn unclear business needs into a clear technical strategy. Fluency in cloud-based data environments (e.g., Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery) and BI tools such as Looker and Tableau. Solid track record establishing data hygiene practices, including version control, code review standards, testing, and documentation, across a team. Great judgment and attention to detail, particularly when balancing competing priorities across two distinct data domains.

 

Additional Qualifications:

 

Experience leading teams in charge of both content and subscriber data simultaneously or leading a team through a merger of previously separate domains. Experience with content rights and licensing data, including availability windows and territory restrictions.

Experience with subscriber lifecycle analytics, including churn modeling, cohort analysis, or LTV calculations.

Proficiency in Python or another scripting language for data transformation or orchestration.

Knowledge with streaming media or direct-to-consumer digital products.

Experience building or scaling anomaly detection systems.

Knowledge of data governance, privacy, and compliance best practices, particularly regarding subscriber PII, billing data, and licensed content.

job.description:
#WeAreParamount on a mission to unleash the power of content… you in?

 Apply to join our new platform initiative and take ownership of building a centralized performance testing automation platform for games development. In this role, you will collaborate with developers, designers, and QA teams to design and deliver a unified system that aggregates performance data from multiple game engines, processes results, and clearly highlights performance issues. 

 You will play a key role in defining the software architecture, database schemas, and overall system experience, while helping to track and visualize optimization progress over time. As this is a brand‑new platform with no prior internal equivalent, you’ll have a unique opportunity to shape its foundations and influence how performance testing is approached across our game development teams. 

 

 

What you will do: 

  • Develop and maintain a platform (applications, integrations and infrastructure) supporting gaming department

  • Partner closely with software architects, game developers, QA, and operations to remove bottlenecks and improve delivery 

  • Build and Maintain CI/CD Pipelines 

  • Script repetitive tasks and develop self-service tools for developers 

  • Design and manage infrastructure 

  • Implement and manage containers, stand up and manage VMs 

  • Implement logging, monitoring, and alerting 

  • Ensure infrastructure is scalable, secure, and reliable. 

 

We are looking for Engineers that: 

  • Are curious, with a desire to learn and the ambition to quickly become a self-reliant, top-notch software engineer,  

  • Value collaboration, knowledge sharing, and contributing to the team's overall effectiveness,  

  • Equally enjoys coding applications and managing infrastructure 

  • Keep up to date with modern web technologies,   

  • Want to actively participate in decision making and fully understand products they work on,   

  • Open to learn new programing languages, 

  • Enjoy working in a team,   

  • Easily and openly communicate in English.  

 

And on the technical side, we need: 

  • 3+ years of experience in software development, build automation, delivery and deployment 

  • Good understanding of concepts like CI/CD, GitOps, configuration management, cloud platforms, version control, automation, monitoring, analytics, containerization, and microservices architecture 

  • Comfortable coding in at least one programing language (preferred: Kotlin, Java, JavaScript, Python, C++/C#) 

  • Experienced in code collaboration in Git, 

  • Experienced in containers orchestration in Kubernetes, 

  • Good knowledge and practical experience managing Cloud infrastructure. OCI is a huge plus. 

  • Experience standing up and maintaining Windows and/or Linux VMs 

  • Bonus: hands-on experience with Unreal Engine 

  • Bonus: hands-on experience scripting in BuildGraph 

  • Bonus: hands-on experience in code collaboration using Perforce 

  

We keep our technologies up-to-date, and have a major impact on the tool set: 

  • CI/CD & Automation: Horde, Jenkins, ArgoCD 

  • Infrastructure & Platform: OCI, Terraform, Ansible 

  • Containers & Virtualization: Kubernetes, Podman, Proxmox, KVM 

  • Observability & Reliability: Prometheus, Grafana, New Relic 

  • Game Development: Unreal Engine 

  • Source Control Management: Perforce, Git 

  • Operating Systems: Linux, Windows 

 

We offer: 

  • Employment contract, 

  • Multisport card + private medical care, 

  • Access to e-learning and self-development platforms, 

  • Office library, 

  • English and Polish language lessons, 

  • We participate in and speak at conferences, also join/ run public meet-ups, 

  • In-house activities: tech talks, hackathons, 

  • You can use 10% of your working time to pursue your personal development, and side projects, 

  • Active global inclusion and CSR groups, 

  • Well located, modern office with lots of amenities – adjustable desks, electronics toolkit, 3D printer ready for you to use, pool table, console, table tennis, massage chair.

Job Title

GSOC Coordinator

Job Description

About The Position | Major Goals and Objectives and Location Requirements:

People Inc. is seeking an experienced GSOC Coordinator to serve as a trusted operational resource within the Global Security Operations Center. This position performs the full range of GSOC operator duties while also supporting advanced enterprise security work involving intelligence, investigations, travel security, executive protection, and crisis management.

Reporting to the Manager, GSOC & Intelligence, the Coordinator operates security systems, manages incidents and communications, conducts research and assessments, and supports sensitive security matters requiring sound judgment, discretion, strong writing, and independent decision-making.

Schedule Requirements:

Full In-Office

In-office Expectations: This position is a fully in-office role due to the nature of the work being done.
 

About The Team | The Team and/or Brand:

The Security team at People Inc. is responsible for ensuring the safety and security of employees, facilities, and assets across all office site locations. The team partners closely with contracted security staff, reception, facilities, event teams, and law enforcement agencies to deliver a consistent and resilient security program.

About The Position’s Contributions:

GSOC and Site Security Operations

  • Operate the GSOC and continuously monitor alarms, CCTV, access control, life-safety systems, and other enterprise security technologies.

  • Receive, assess, document, and coordinate the response to security incidents, emergencies, system alerts, and requests for assistance.

  • Dispatch security personnel, maintain communications with field operations, and ensure timely escalation to Security Management and appropriate business partners.

  • Prepare and distribute mass notifications, emergency communications, incident updates, and other enterprise security messages when authorized.

  • Support access-control administration, video review, incident documentation, daily logs, shift turnover, and security-system troubleshooting.

Intelligence and Investigative Support

  • Conduct open-source intelligence research, social media monitoring, threat-actor research, and other authorized intelligence collection in support of active security matters.

  • Assist with threat assessments, workplace violence concerns, criminal and administrative investigations, background research, and investigative case support.

  • Support executive and brand threat monitoring by identifying, documenting, and escalating information that may indicate risk to employees, executives, offices, events, or company operations.

  • Produce clear, accurate, and timely incident reports, intelligence summaries, investigative memoranda, and executive-ready briefing materials.

Travel, Executive, and Crisis Support

  • Monitor employee and executive travel, assess destination and geopolitical risk, and support traveler accountability during incidents or emergencies.

  • Provide operational and intelligence support for executive travel, protective operations, corporate events, and other elevated-risk activities.

  • Monitor global incidents, severe weather, civil unrest, geopolitical developments, and other events that could affect company personnel or operations.

  • Support crisis activations through situational awareness, communications, incident tracking, escalation, and preparation of situation reports.

Program and Operational Support

  • Work closely with Security Operations personnel to coordinate field response, information sharing, and operational support during incidents and special events.

  • Support the Manager, GSOC & Intelligence with program documentation, procedures, audits, metrics, training materials, and special projects.

  • Handle sensitive company, employee, investigative, and executive information with discretion and in accordance with established protocols.

  • Maintain a professional, service-oriented approach when assisting employees, executives, visitors, law enforcement, vendors, and business partners.

The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements:

Education:

Bachelor's degree in criminal justice, intelligence studies, security management, emergency management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in law enforcement, intelligence, investigations, corporate security, military service, emergency management, or a related public safety field.

  • Demonstrated experience with investigations, intelligence research, threat assessments, analytical research, or other complex security work beyond routine monitoring and dispatch.

  • Ability to independently operate a command center environment, manage competing priorities, assess incomplete information, and make timely, defensible decisions.

  • Excellent written communication and report-writing skills, including the ability to organize complex information into concise operational or executive summaries.

  • Strong judgment, discretion, attention to detail, and ability to handle sensitive or confidential information.

  • Working knowledge of CCTV, access control, alarm monitoring, incident management, mass notification, and common GSOC or physical security technologies.

  • Strong computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office and the ability to learn investigative, intelligence, travel-monitoring, and security-system platforms.

  • Ability to successfully complete required pre-employment screening and obtain required certifications after hire.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior law enforcement experience, particularly in investigations, intelligence, detective operations, emergency response, or command-center functions.

  • Experience in a GSOC, Security Operations Center, Emergency Operations Center, Fusion Center, intelligence unit, investigative unit, or comparable environment.

  • Experience with OSINT, social media research, threat management, travel security, executive protection support, or crisis monitoring.

  • Relevant certifications such as APP, CPP, PSP, PCI, First Aid, CPR, AED, or similar credentials.

job.description:
At Warner Music Group, we’re a global collective of music makers and music lovers, tech innovators and inspired entrepreneurs, game-changing creatives and passionate team members. Here, we turn dreams into stardom and audiences into fans. We are guided by three core values that underpin everything we do across all our diverse businesses: 

  • Curiosity: We do our best work when we’re immersing ourselves in culture and breaking through barriers. Curiosity is the driving force behind creativity and ingenuity. It fuels innovation, and innovation is the key to our future. 

  • Collaboration: Making music and bringing it to the world is all about the power of originality amplified by teamwork. A great idea, like a great song, travels globally. We ignite passions and build connections across our diverse community of artists, songwriters, partners, and fans.

  • Commitment: We pursue excellence for our team and our talent. Everything in music starts with a leap into the unknown, and we’re committed to keeping the faith, acting with integrity, and delivering on our promises.

WMG is home to a wide range of artists, musicians, and songwriters that fuel our success. That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone.  We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.

Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.
 

Job Title: 

Vice President, Strategy

About you:

job.title: Staff Software Engineer
job.description:
1 big thing: Axios is a growth-focused media company helping people get smarter, faster, on what matters. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer—a senior, hands-on individual contributor—to lead architecture and delivery for Axios’ core products across multiple teams using strong product-engineering and AI-native practices.

Why it matters: Axios delivers clear, trustworthy news to millions of readers. You’ll be anchored to a product area while shaping full-stack systems and technical direction across multiple teams and connected systems. This is not a people-management role.

AI is core to how we build. You’ll use coding agents throughout implementation, testing, review, debugging, documentation, and operations while remaining accountable for architecture, quality, security, and product outcomes. Staff impact comes from sustained scope, judgment, and results—not tool use alone.

You’ll work with product managers, designers, engineers, and leaders to shape plans, align dependencies, resolve ambiguity, build resilient systems, and help others make better technical decisions.

Responsibilities:

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll lead reliable product and platform work across Axios’ frontend and backend systems. You’ll remain hands-on while driving multi-quarter initiatives, improving technical coherence, and using agentic practices to accelerate delivery. Key responsibilities include:

  • Cross-team technical leadership: Lead mission-critical or high-risk initiatives spanning teams and connected systems. Frame problems, align ownership and dependencies, make tradeoffs explicit, and drive production adoption.
  • Architecture and design: Own architecture for a product area and scalable boundaries across frontend, APIs, data, and production systems. Lead design reviews and establish standards within your sphere of influence.
  • Hands-on system ownership: Own the technical direction and long-term evolution of key systems while writing and reviewing code, prototyping, debugging, leading migrations, and operating services in production.
  • AI-enabled product and engineering: Identify where models, agents, retrieval, or automation create value. Build reusable capabilities with measurable behavior, guardrails, and judgment about when conventional software is better.
  • Quality, reliability, and incident leadership: Improve testing, performance, observability, security, and operational readiness. Anticipate systemic risks, address technical debt, and help lead resolution and learning during critical production issues.
  • Technical leadership and mentorship: Mentor mid- and senior-level engineers across teams, spread systems thinking and design patterns, and build alignment through proposals, reviews, and influence without authority.
  • Product and technical strategy: Partner with product, design, and engineering leaders to shape the product-area roadmap, align dependencies, and connect technical investment to reader, editorial, and business outcomes.

Skills:

The ideal candidate is a staff-level engineer with sustained multi-team impact, deep expertise in a relevant domain, broad systems thinking, and a commitment to user experience, reliability, scalability, maintainable code, and effective AI-enabled practice. You should have:

  • Experience: Typically 7+ years in professional software development, or equivalent sustained Staff-level impact, including leading complex initiatives across multiple teams or systems.
  • AI-native development: Hands-on experience using agentic coding tools—such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or comparable tools—to complete meaningful, multi-step software work, rather than only generating snippets or using autocomplete.
  • Agent direction and context: Ability to write clear strategies, specifications, and acceptance criteria; provide context; scope complex work; decide what to delegate; and redirect incomplete or incorrect approaches.
  • Verification and engineering judgment: Ability to review AI-generated code critically, validate assumptions, identify security, scalability, and maintainability risks, and catch plausible but wrong solutions. You understand that AI raises the importance of sound architecture, testing, and human judgment.
  • Frontend development: Hands-on experience building production interfaces with JavaScript or TypeScript and React, preferably with Next.js, plus judgment to guide frontend architecture across teams.
  • Backend development: Hands-on experience building production services and APIs. Our backend systems use Go and Python, and you should be able to shape reliable service boundaries and work effectively in or learn either language.
  • Data fundamentals: Experience with relational databases, SQL, schema design, transactions, and migrations.
  • Quality and security: Experience with testing, accessibility, input validation, authentication, authorization, and web security practices, plus the ability to raise standards across teams.
  • Engineering judgment: Ability to operate independently in ambiguity, identify high-leverage problems, align teams, make sound tradeoffs, and connect decisions to product and business goals—including when AI is not the right tool.
  • Communication: Ability to build alignment through clear proposals and reasoning, communicate risks and tradeoffs across functions, and drive clarity during disagreement.
  • Continuous learning: Curiosity about changing models, tools, and practices, paired with an evidence-based approach. You share useful patterns, identify what fails, and make others more effective.

We’ll be even more excited if you have:

  • Experience building production AI-enabled features using model APIs, structured outputs, tool or function calling, retrieval, or agent workflows.
  • Experience evaluating and operating AI-enabled systems through regression tests, evaluation harnesses, tracing, feedback loops, model or prompt versioning, cost and latency monitoring, or human-review paths.
  • Experience extending AI development environments through MCP servers, agent tools, repository instructions, reusable skills or plugins, custom workflows, or automated code review.
  • Led a multi-team architecture, platform, migration, or modernization initiative from problem framing through production adoption.
  • Owned critical systems through incidents, scaling challenges, and long-term architectural evolution.
  • Drove adoption of technical standards, reusable tools, or platform capabilities across multiple teams.
  • Mentored experienced engineers and helped improve technical judgment beyond your immediate team.
  • Experience with CMS, publishing, media, subscription, search, or other consumer-facing products.
  • Production experience with Go or Python and distributed systems using gRPC, cloud infrastructure, containers, queues, CI/CD, or similar technologies.

What success looks like:

  • Cross-team delivery: You drive multi-quarter initiatives from problem framing through production adoption, aligning dependencies and ownership to produce durable outcomes.
  • Engineering leverage: Teams deliver more effectively because of the standards, tools, architecture, documentation, and context you create. You establish safe, repeatable AI patterns where they add value.
  • System health: Key systems become more reliable, scalable, secure, observable, and easier to change. You reduce systemic risk and improve incident prevention and response.
  • Product-area impact: Your decisions support Axios’ readers, products, editorial workflows, and business goals within the teams and systems you influence.
  • Organizational technical leadership: Engineers across teams make better decisions through your mentorship, proposals, reviews, and example. You remain a hands-on IC who multiplies others’ effectiveness.

 

Starting salary for this role is in the range of $165,000 - $215,000 and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. This range does not include other compensation benefits. Axios' compensation philosophy takes into account the cost of labor differentials across the country. Because this is a remote-optional job posting, this salary range takes into account all possible locations within the United States, but candidates will only be eligible for the salary range for their location.

Axios is committed to embracing artificial intelligence as a core part of how we work. All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. We invest in ongoing learning to ensure every employee is equipped to responsibly and effectively integrate AI into their daily workflows.

What Axios brings to the table besides salary:

  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Robust PPO and High Deductible health insurance options on the Blue Cross Blue Shield network
  • Employer Health Savings Account (HSA) contribution for the high deductible health plan option
  • Dental and vision coverage
  • Primary caregiver 12-week paid leave
  • Birth-givers will have an additional 6-8 weeks depending on type of delivery, for a total of 18-20 weeks continuous leave
  • Generous vacation policy, plus holidays
  • One mental health day per quarter
  • Annual learning and development stipend
  • $100 monthly work-from-home stipend
  • Tele-mental health services through Headspace
  • OneMedical membership, including tele-health services
  • Personal health advocacy resources through HealthAdvocate
  • Inclusive fertility, hormonal health and family forming benefits through Carrot Fertility
  • Access to the Axios “Family Fund”, which was created to allow employees to request financial support when facing financial hardship or emergencies
  • Increased work flexibility for parents and caretakers
  • Virtual company-sponsored social events
  • A strong and positive work environment
  • A commitment to an open, inclusive, and diverse work culture

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement 

Axios is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. 

This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. Axios makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

job.title: Privacy Engineering Lead
job.description: About Suno We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world. Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible. Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA). About the Role We're looking for a Privacy Engineering Lead to build Suno's privacy and AI governance function from scratch. You'll set the technical direction for how we handle data and permissions across our platform, models, and agents — building the infrastructure that enforces policy at the point of use and verifies outcomes like retention and deletion. You'll partner closely with Legal and Product while hiring and growing your own engineering team to scale this work across the company. What You'll Do Build the policy foundations for how Suno handles data, permitted uses, and AI, in partnership with Legal. Own data discovery, classification, and permissions mapping across our product, analytics, and vendor systems. Design and operate governance controls across our products, data platforms, models, and agents, enforcing consent, access, and data-sharing rules. Lead verified user rights operations, including access, correction, deletion, and consent management, partnering with Product on self-service tools. Hire and grow a dedicated privacy engineering team, giving this work the focused ownership it needs to scale. Help make responsible data handling part of how Suno builds every new model and feature, in service of making creative fulfillment a daily reality for everyone. What You'll Need Must-Haves 8-10 years hands-on software engineering experience, with the technical depth to help build and ship enforcement infrastructure yourself, not only define policy for others to implement. Deep experience in privacy engineering or data governance, including working familiarity with regulatory frameworks like GDPR and CCPA. Experience as an engineering manager who has maintained real technical depth, or as a Staff+ engineer ready to grow into people management. Nice-to-Haves Experience with AI/ML governance, model evaluation pipelines, or generative AI systems. Background at a consumer tech company at scale, or one with a significant European user base. Prior experience as an early or founding privacy/governance hire at a growing company. Work Location Policy This role is expected to work from the designated Suno office 5 days a week, per Suno's company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience. Additional Notes Applicants must be eligible to work in the US. Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees Company Equity Package 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k) Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options) 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave Creative Education Stipend Generous Commuter Allowance In-Office Lunch (5 days per week) Compensation: The annual salary range for this role is $276,960 - $363,510 + target equity + benefits (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k) Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.
